# Interview pack: Brightwave, AI Engineer (screening, standard, 30 min)

## Competencies
- c1 Shipping LLM products: "You will ship LLM-powered features from prototype to production."
- c2 Ownership and communication: "You own problems end to end and explain trade-offs clearly."
- c3 Evaluation and reliability: "You measure quality with evals and keep latency and cost under control."

## Evidence about the candidate
- e1 (project) Built Verse, a macOS meeting assistant: a Swift app plus a Python brain that streams Claude answers to a notch card while the call is running.
- e2 (metric) At Lantern, cut invoice entry time from 11 minutes to 2 minutes per document by adding an LLM extraction step with a human review screen.
- e3 (project) Published Trailhead, an iOS running and cycling app, on the App Store; wrote the backend and ran 4 ad experiments.

## Questions
- q1 opener [c2] (target 60-120 s): Tell me a bit about yourself and what brought you to this role.
- q2 behavioural [c1, c3] (target 60-120 s): Describe a time you took an LLM feature from prototype to production.
- q3 motivation [c2] (target 30-60 s): Why Brightwave?
- q4 technical [c3] (target 90-150 s): How would you keep latency and cost under control in a streaming LLM feature?

## Rubric
- c1: 1 No concrete product shipped. / 3 Shipped something, vague on production concerns. / 5 Prototype to production with named trade-offs and results.
- c2: 1 Rambling, no ownership. / 3 Clear but generic. / 5 Owns outcomes and explains trade-offs crisply.
- c3: 1 No measurement. / 3 Mentions metrics without numbers. / 5 Evals, latency and cost with numbers.
